facts.claim: Writing GLB/glTF 2.0 by hand is feasible with Foundation only. GLB = 12-byte header (magic 0x46546C67 'glTF', version 2, total length, all uint32 little endian) + chunk0 JSON (chunkLength, chunkType 0x4E4F534A, JSON padded with 0x20 spaces to 4 bytes) + chunk1 BIN (chunkType 0x004E4942, zero-padded to 4 bytes). buffers[0] must have no 'uri' (it is the BIN chunk). Minimal JSON: asset.version '2.0', scene/scenes/nodes/meshes[primitives{attributes{POSITION,NORMAL,TEXCOORD_0,COLOR_0},indices,material}], accessors (componentType 5126 FLOAT, 5125 UNSIGNED_INT, 5123 UNSIGNED_SHORT, 5121 UNSIGNED_BYTE with normalized:true; POSITION accessor needs min/max), bufferViews (byteOffset/byteLength, target 34962/34963 optional), images[{bufferView, mimeType 'image/png'|'image/jpeg'}], textures[{source, sampler?}], materials[{pbrMetallicRoughness{baseColorTexture{index}, metallicFactor 0, roughnessFactor 1}}], optional extensionsUsed ['KHR_materials_unlit'] for baked scans.
facts.api: JSONSerialization / JSONEncoder + Data(append:) with withUnsafeBytes of [Float]/[UInt32]; UIImage.pngData()/jpegData(compressionQuality:) for the embedded texture
facts.notes: glTF is +Y up, right-handed like ARKit/RoomPlan, so no axis swap is needed (unlike Y-up to Z-up for some CAD tools). Use uint32 indices when vertex count > 65535. Keep bufferView byte offsets 4-aligned (pad each view). Texture coords: glTF UV origin is top-left, Metal/ARKit capture UVs may need v = 1 - v; verify visually once in a viewer.

facts.claim: OBJ, STL and PLY are trivial text/binary formats that need no framework: OBJ = 'v x y z', 'vn', 'vt u v', 'f a/b/c ...' (1-based), 'mtllib'/'usemtl'; MTL = 'newmtl', 'Kd r g b', 'map_Kd texture.jpg' (relative path); binary STL = 80-byte header + uint32 triangle count + 50 bytes per triangle (normal 3f, 3 vertices 9f, uint16 attribute) little endian, no colors; PLY as above. Writing them ourselves removes every ModelIO uncertainty and works on all iOS versions.
facts.notes: STL has no units; CAD tools assume mm, so scale metres to mm (x1000) at export and say so in the UI. OBJ/MTL/textures must be zipped together for sharing (see zip fact).

facts.claim: Vector PDF at a chosen scale: UIGraphicsPDFRenderer(bounds:format:) with UIGraphicsPDFRendererFormat().documentInfo (kCGPDFContextTitle/Author/kCGPDFContextMediaBox keys) and writePDF(to:withActions:) or pdfData(actions:). Inside the actions closure call context.beginPage() or beginPage(withBounds:pageInfo:) per page and draw with context.cgContext (CGContext: scaleBy/translateBy for the plan scale, addLine, strokePath, NSAttributedString.draw(at:) for text). Minimal DXF that CAD tools open: for R12 (HEADER $ACADVER = AC1009) only the ENTITIES section is formally required ('0
SECTION
2
ENTITIES
...
0
ENDSEC
0
EOF'), and entities are LINE (10/20/30, 11/21/31), CIRCLE (10/20/30, 40), ARC (40, 50 start, 51 end angles in degrees CCW), TEXT (10/20/30, 40 height, 1 string, optional 50 rotation), POLYLINE (66=1, 70 flag 1=closed) + VERTEX ... + SEQEND. LWPOLYLINE does not exist in R12; it needs R2000 (AC1015) files, which AutoCAD requires to have HEADER ($ACADVER, $HANDSEED), CLASSES, TABLES (LAYER with at least layer '0', LTYPE with BYBLOCK/BYLAYER/CONTINUOUS, STYLE and DIMSTYLE with STANDARD, VPORT may be empty), BLOCKS, ENTITIES, OBJECTS, plus unique handles (group 5) on every entity/table record and 100 subclass markers (AcDbEntity, AcDbPolyline). LWPOLYLINE codes: 100 AcDbPolyline, 90 vertex count (must be the first tag after the subclass marker or AutoCAD will not close it), 70 flags (1 = closed), 43 constant width, 10/20 per vertex, 42 bulge per vertex (optional), 38 elevation. Layer on any entity is group 8; color group 62 (ACI 1-255, 256 = BYLAYER).
facts.notes: Recommendation: emit R12/AC1009 with a HEADER ($ACADVER AC1009, $INSUNITS 6 = metres or 4 = mm, $EXTMIN/$EXTMAX) + TABLES/LAYER (0 LAYER, 2 name, 70 0, 62 color, 6 CONTINUOUS) + ENTITIES using LINE/POLYLINE+VERTEX+SEQEND/TEXT/CIRCLE/ARC. R12 with a LAYER table is what LibreCAD, QCAD, AutoCAD, Revit import and SketchUp all accept and it needs no handles. Only go to AC1015 if bulged LWPOLYLINEs are demanded. Units: write metres or millimetres consistently and set $INSUNITS. LWPOLYLINE table verified at https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2017/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-748FC305-F3F2-4F74-825A-61F04D757A50.htm

facts.claim: Apple has no public ZIP-writing API on iOS (Archive/AppleArchive framework only writes .aar; Apple staff: use libarchive/third party). The documented NSFileCoordinator .forUploading behaviour is that reading a DIRECTORY with that option hands the accessor block a temporary file containing the zipped contents of the directory; the temp file is unlinked when the block returns, so it must be moved/copied inside the block. This is Apple-documented behaviour (not a hack) and Apple DTS (Quinn) published the pattern in 2021; the archive always contains the top-level folder name as its root entry and there is no control over compression or entry names.
facts.availability: iOS 8.0+ (forUploading), NSFileCoordinator iOS 5+; still in use in 2024 write-ups, no report of it breaking on iOS 17/18
facts.notes: Second sources: forum 681770 and 688165 (DTS). Pattern: stage the export into a folder named exactly like the wanted archive root (e.g. 'Kitchen-scan/'), coordinate(readingItemAt: folder, options: [.forUploading]) and FileManager.moveItem(at: zipURL, to: Exports/Kitchen-scan.zip) inside the block. The call is synchronous; run it off the main thread. A tiny store-only ZIP writer (local file headers + central directory, CRC32 via zlib's crc32 from the system libz, compress with Compression framework COMPRESSION_ZLIB raw deflate) is ~150 lines if we ever need control over entry names.

gotchas: MDLAsset.export never writes USDZ on iOS (canExportFileExtension('usdz') == false) and its usdc/usda output has been reported material-less/broken; the only native USDZ writers are SCNScene.write(to:) and RoomPlan's CapturedRoom/CapturedStructure export.

SceneKit (SCNScene, write(to:), SCNSceneExportDelegate, sceneWithMDLAsset:) is marked deprecated in the iOS 26 SDK. It compiles with warnings; isolate it in one SceneKitExporter.swift so the rest of the code stays SceneKit-free and the warning is contained.

SCNScene.write(to:) usdz: write to a temp directory then moveItem (sandbox/second-call bug producing a 2 KB garbage file), and only call it from the main thread after the scene has been set up; test twice in a row in the first CI build.

ModelIO OBJ export writes the .mtl only when every submesh has a non-nil MDLMaterial; whether it emits map_Kd for texture samplers is unverified. Own OBJ+MTL writer is ~60 lines and deterministic; prefer it.

ModelIO PLY export is not in Apple's current supported-export list and cannot read binary PLY on import; write PLY ourselves (binary little endian with uchar red/green/blue) and, if we ever re-import, accept only our own files.

NSFileCoordinator .forUploading zip: the URL is valid only inside the accessor block (moveItem inside it), it is synchronous (run on a background queue), and the archive root is the folder name; there is no public API to zip individual files with custom paths, so stage the export folder layout exactly as it should appear in the zip.

ShareLink with FileRepresentation runs the exporting closure lazily and needs the file to survive until the sheet closes; keep exports in Documents/<project>/Exports rather than a temp dir that is purged, and give ShareLink a SharePreview so the sheet does not show a blank row.

Files app visibility needs both UIFileSharingEnabled and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace; on iOS 18 an empty Documents folder may not appear and a CFBundleVersion bump refreshes stale metadata. Sideloadly re-signs every 7 days with the same bundle id so the container (and exports) survive.
QLPreviewController: return `url as QLPreviewItem`, not ARQuickLookPreviewItem(fileAt:), for files outside the bundle; QuickLook previews only USDZ (plus PDF/PNG), not OBJ/GLB/PLY/STL.

UIGraphicsPDFRenderer works in points with a top-left origin; scale drawing = scaleBy(x: ptPerMetre, y: -ptPerMetre) after translating to the page bottom if the plan uses +Y up. STL has no units (CAD assumes mm), DXF needs $INSUNITS; decide 'export in millimetres' once for all CAD formats and keep metres for glTF/USDZ/OBJ.
PhotogrammetrySession on iOS supports only .reduced detail and USDZ output, and needs LiDAR + A14+; wrap it behind PhotogrammetrySession.isSupported / ObjectCaptureSession.isSupported.
R12 DXF has no LWPOLYLINE; use POLYLINE/VERTEX/SEQEND, or switch to AC1015 which then requires HEADER/CLASSES/TABLES/BLOCKS/OBJECTS skeleton plus unique handles on every record.
recommendations: Own the mesh exporters: write OBJ+MTL, binary PLY (with vertex colors), binary STL and GLB writers in a small Foundation-only `Exporters` module operating on our own Mesh struct (positions, normals, uvs, colors, indices, optional texture Data). Zero framework risk, exact control over units/axes, and the writers are trivially unit-testable on CI (macOS runner can run `swift test` on a pure-Swift target).

Use native writers only where they add real value: RoomPlan CapturedRoom.export(to:exportOptions: [.parametric, .mesh]) plus the iOS 17 metadata JSON for the architectural USDZ, and SCNScene.write(to: tmp.usdz) for a textured USDZ (build SCNGeometry from our Mesh, SCNMaterial.diffuse.contents = UIImage, write to temp, move).
